notes: The federation's own first broadcast, and the night all four of its founding championships were filled. Three one-night tournaments were run from the Montreal Forum — twelve men in singles, six teams, six in the All-Jobber bracket — with the singles final doubling as the North American title match under the tournament's own rule that the runner-up took the second belt. First-round byes went to Johnny Vicious, Death, Bobby Windsor and Plague Dog in singles, to the Russians and the Masked Missiles in tag, and to the Wolfman and Baron Von Klaw in the All-Jobber bracket; byes are recorded here in prose and are not structured as matches. The four-man announce desk, the ring announcer and the interview show are all in place from this issue on.

notes: The federation's first SuperCard, billed from Wembley Stadium in front of a capacity crowd of 85,000. Seven matches, three of them six-man elimination bouts. The card was announced for Thursday 16 May and broadcast here two days later; the date recorded is the broadcast's own. The announce desk states on air that only two matches on the card counted towards the federation's Hype ratings, handicap and Survivor Series matches being excluded by the president's own ruling. The main event ended on a mask reveal: the Masked Avengers were the former World Tag-Team Champions, Crime and Punishment. The card closes on the federation's own copyright line.

Cowboy Kevin Puckett made the Black Knight submit to the spinning toehold at 3:51; Brewster Cogburn put Puckett through the announce table and he was counted out at 6:34; Sledge Hammer threw Cogburn into the ringpost and he was counted out at 8:37; Baron Von Klaw pinned Bobby Windsor at 14:01; and Von Klaw took the Klaw hold on a bleeding Sledge Hammer at 14:27, the referee stopping it. Sole survivor: Baron Von Klaw, who had pinned the World Champion.

“A Modest Proposal”, a handicap brass-knuckles match of Captain Necropolis's own design, with the knuckles hidden inside a doll filled with cherry jello. Necropolis got the knuckles, missed with them, and Horowitz went over the top rope into Club Anarchy's own fans and was counted out at 0:59.

A surprise attraction. Admiral Chekov beamed in the BattleCruisers — Klingon Disrupter and the Romulan Mauler, billed as legends of the old PWGA — for one night only; the Romulan Mauler's top-rope Plasma Torpedo finished El Cheapo at 4:36. The broadcast's own aside notes that La Corrida stayed on as a jobber team managed by the federation itself.

A Flag match and a six-man elimination match. The Allied Forces swept the Jungle: the Patriot splashed the Spewmaster out at 5:00, Chief Tomahawk dropped an elbow on Panther, and Sargent Glasnost finished Bear with the Japanese Armlock. Club Anarchy interfered in disguise mid-match, dressed as Bear and as Glasnost. Afterwards the Spewmaster handed the flags to the winners and spat mist in his own manager's face, breaking up the Jungle.
Sword and Shield's federation debut against a team they said they had fought countless times in the WeWF. Destruction superplexed Angus Campbell and bridged for the fall at 14:42.

notes: THE RENAME. The post's own subject line reads “UFWS Report #11 (UFWS = PWGeA)” and its body opens “the twelfth UFWS Report; actually the first one under that name.” Report #11 itself does not survive, and this issue reports around its gap: it names three championships that changed hands inside it — the World title to Running Eagle Feather, the North American title to Brewster Cogburn, and the World Tag-Team titles to the Shadow Assassins — without carrying the matches. The Four Corners arrive; the Mage's Gallery's feud with the Hellhound opens with a fireball on the interview stage. TWO CORRECTIONS THE DOCUMENT MAKES AGAINST ITSELF, recorded rather than smoothed: the results desk calls the first tag-team tournament match a “first semi-final” while the colour commentator in the same issue calls both of that week's tournament matches quarter-finals, and the bracket the next two issues run confirms the quarter-final reading; and the new World Tag-Team Champions are stated to forfeit their own tournament match, which is how the American Guerilla reached the semi-finals.

matches.note: World Tag-Team Championship. notes: The federation's second and last surviving SuperCard, billed from the Northlands Coliseum in Edmonton and running against the WWF's Summer Slam by its own commentary's admission. Seven matches and one that never started: the full cage match between Warren Hammer and the Hellhound was called off when the Hellhound ambushed Hammer on the aisle and strangled him with a rope, and Hammer left in an ambulance. The night ends on the federation's own copyright line under its new name.

matches.note: Opening match. The Aztec Mummy submitted to Ricky Dangerous's Boston Crab; the announce desk made the Shadow Assassins No.1 contenders on the result.

matches.stipulation: Twelve-man battle royal; the winner to challenge for the World Heavyweight Championship later the same night
matches.note: A twelve-man battle royal for a World title shot later the same night. Randy Hurricane went first, eliminated by his own stablemate Bamm Bamm Gigolow in league with Angus Campbell; then the Warden, the World Champion himself (dumped by Death and Destruction), Angus Campbell, Bamm Bamm Gigolow, Ford Firepower, the Plague Dog, Death, Mr. Mercury and Lightning Bolt. John Girder eliminated Destruction last to win it.

A War Games match — two rings inside a cage, the two managers stranded on a twenty-foot scaffold with the only way down being into the ring. Jack Moran throttled Smooth with a noose on the scaffold and backdropped Billy Thunder twenty feet into the ring; a second Jack Moran then ran out from the dressing room. The Moran outside the ring threw in the towel to save Brewster Cogburn from a spiked piledriver. Both masks came off afterwards: the Masked Avenger was Wilhelm Panzer and the Moran was Baron Von Klaw.

The Soviets' last match in North America before being recalled home for the Zampolit's treason trial. The Wolfman bashed both Soviets' heads together and pinned Bear. Their six-man police escort in gray coats turned out to be the All-Jobber Confederation.

matches.stipulation: Romulan Warbird match — steel cage, brass knuckles suspended, all members must escape
matches.note: A Romulan Warbird match: a cage, brass knuckles hanging from the ceiling, and no win until every member of a team had escaped. Jimmy Vendetta took the knuckles from Dr. Lethe and got out; Captain Necropolis climbed out; and with the Patriot and the Romulan Mauler on top of the cage, Vendetta climbed back up and knocked the Patriot back into the ring with the knuckles, letting Dr. Lethe touch the floor first.

matches.stipulation: North American Tag-Team Championship tournament final, for the inaugural title
matches.note: NORTH AMERICAN TAG-TEAM CHAMPIONSHIP, tournament final for the vacant title. The Hunter fell on Chief Tomahawk off a Wizard dropkick for the three count, and the New Mystics became the first North American Tag-Team Champions — holding belts in two federations at once, by the announce desk's own claim. Hammer and Sickle shook hands with them afterwards.

MAIN EVENT, World Heavyweight Championship, against the winner of the battle royal. Girder kicked out of the shoulder throw — the first man ever to do so, the announce desk said — and Sledge Hammer pinned him with a small package. The champion retained.

The next report was promised for the following Thursday or Friday and does not survive.
